what_happened: Dispatch asserted memory-retrieve.sh is already dead (sole call site swapped), but a repo-wide grep found 25 live call sites across 12 extensions' SKILL.md Stage 4a blocks (python, web, cslib x2, latex, epidemiology, email, z3, nvim, nix, rust, books, typst) that still invoke it directly, independent of the orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh call site task 496 swapped. sapience-retrieve.sh is a confirmed drop-in replacement (identical signature and output envelope) so the fix is mechanical, but Part C's file-touch scope must widen to cover all 25 sites or the 'no remaining reference' verification bullet will fail.

sapience-retrieve.sh was confirmed to be byte-for-byte API-compatible with memory-retrieve.sh (same 3-positional-arg signature, same <memory-context> envelope, same deployed path), making the 25-site Part C cleanup a mechanical rename rather than a logic rewrite.

Part B's six-sub-mode deletion (report/purge/merge/compress/refine/gc) is not a clean six-section removal: the Scoring Engine's composite-score and health_score formulas must be retained because the surviving 'auto' sub-mode still consumes them for its own health_score recalculation, while only the Health Report Template and Maintenance Candidate Classification table are safe to delete outright. Flagged in the research report for the plan phase.

Plan-phase live probe settled the Part C2 keep-vs-replace sub-decision with evidence instead of judgment: an unfiltered mcp__sapience__sapience_search returned a KO whose provenance carries [repo:nvim] alongside untagged KOs, proving the repo tag narrows only reads that request the source= filter. A tagged write is therefore strictly more reachable than an untagged one, so replacing the untagged sapience_wrapup call rather than keeping both halves permanent unreviewed write volume at zero reachability cost.

Re-derivation at plan time found the declared file_scope materially narrower than the work the task requires: the 25 extension Stage 4a call sites (confirmed live, 25 of 25 still invoking the retired retrieval script), memory/EXTENSION.md, memory/commands/distill.md, the four deleted submode pattern files, core/manifest.json and roughly a dozen prose-reference files are all absent from it. The plan declares them via per-phase Files to modify blocks so plan-file-scope-harvest.sh widens file_scope at plan postflight.

Caught a self-inflicted false-failure before it shipped: the plan's first draft encoded the dispatch's '.memory/ is present and unmodified' bullet as 'git status --porcelain .memory/ is empty', but .memory/memory-index.json already carried a pre-existing modification at dispatch start, so that criterion would have failed on state the task never created and invited an implementer to 'repair' it by writing to a tree the task holds read-only. All four occurrences were rewritten as a comparison against an explicitly recorded starting baseline. Also caught by the artifact validator in the same pass: two Tier Justification lines named suites that suite_selection_select does not actually return for their phases' touched paths; Phase 4 was re-declared as a justified non-final full and Phase 5 as prose with a gate subset.

verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 reported FAIL after Phase 2 edits, but the failure is confined to 'core' and 'lean' extension deploy-drift (git-commit-scoped.sh, lint-routing-wiring.sh, known-failures.txt, test-routing-resolution.sh, lean-plan-compliance-check.sh) owned by concurrent sibling tasks 423/461, not to this task's file_scope. The 'memory' extension row (this task's own Phase 2 edits) reports PASS. Gate 4 (task-reference lint) passed cleanly.
